Seems that implicit casting in UInt128 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/74001) has broke source gen
Per https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/74001#issuecomment-1216948508 I'll add extra overloads to fix the build break

Closing this PR. See my comment here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/73500#issuecomment-1220589391 - we need more data about usage of (U)Int128 to make sure we're not adding very niche overloads.

issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: System.Text.Json (U)Int128 related APIs
comments: What makes JSON special here? We didn't add any APIs to `BinaryReader`/`BinaryWriter` either. Is this just for completeness or is anyone requesting this?

@terrajobst Per my comment https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/73500#issuecomment-1220589391 we'll not  be shipping these APIs in 7.0 timeline.

I assumed that if this met bar to be added to System namespace and System.Runtime it has high expected usage but seems that might not be true. JSON felt like more use facing than BinaryReader/Writer.

review_comments: Nit: consider making a partial class with the .NET 7 specific functionality rather than using compile conditionals.

I think keeping them grouped as is with extra conditional is fine since extracting them to extra file would be inconsistent with current grouping.

Perhaps current grouping is not ideal and it would be better to split those file into something along the lines of i.e.:
UtfJsonWriter.int.cs
UtfJsonWriter.uint.cs

Possibly we could even generate those files fully or partially but I'll leave this out of scope for this PR since there is a high chance this will get ported to 7.0 and I'd prefer to avoid churning
Should this one be ifdef'ed as well?
It could be but it will be unnecessarily over-complicated. I generally agree with @eiriktsarpalis's response here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/69160/files#r871454257

Do we need to add support to these other types? For `Date/TimeOnly`, serializer support was deemed sufficient because most JSON-processing of those types would be via the serializer. `BigInteger` is also not supported, not even by the serializer.

BigInteger lives in System.Numerics while Int128/UInt128 live in System and is now part of BCL. My understanding is that new 128-bit integers are on pair with existing 64-bit. Also having this supported only by serializes means that number handling will be only partially supported for them

> Also having this supported only by serializes means that number handling will be only partially supported for them

Why is this? Number handling is surfaced (and implemented) only at the serializer level IIRC.
